rows.name: flagpole shaft
rows.notes: World 1-1 end-of-level flagpole, left half of the shaft. CHR $1A2 = a single 1px vertical line in the rightmost column (index 1), all other pixels transparent - so the pole's 2px-wide line is this tile's right edge plus CHR $1A3's left edge. Placed in the live nametable as tile id $A2 (tile column 12 of the flagpole block) at every 8px row from nametable row 6 down to row 20. Palette 0 (slot 1 $29 lime green = the pole line). PROOF: get_tile_at_pixel(232,150) = tile_id 163 ($A3) / palette 0 / chr_tile 419 / background_pattern_addr 4096, screen box (232,144); read_nametable 0 at (12,3) 3x18 shows rows 6-20 as A2 A3; get_region object mode at (232,150) returned background palette 0 slot 1, 128 connected pixels in a 2x64 box (231,118)-(232,181) across CHR 0x1A2/0x1A3.
rows.why: the flagpole beside the staircase with the flag at its top in this screenshot; CHR $1A2/$1A3 render as the one-pixel shaft halves, $12F/$13D as the ball halves, sprite $7E/$7F as the pennant

rows.name: flagpole shaft
rows.notes: World 1-1 end-of-level flagpole, right half of the shaft. CHR $1A3 = a single 1px vertical line in the leftmost column (index 1), the rest transparent. Together with CHR $1A2 (line on its right edge) it draws the pole's 2px-wide vertical line. Nametable tile id $A3 at tile column 13 of the flagpole block, rows 6-20; palette 0 slot 1 $29 lime green. PROOF: get_tile_at_pixel(232,150) returned tile_id 163 = $A3, palette 0, chr_tile 419, screen box (232,144), background_pattern_addr 4096; read_tile 419 shows the index-1 left column; read_nametable 0 (12,3) 3x18 = column13 A3 for rows 6-20; get_region object mode (232,150) = 2x64 box across CHR 0x1A2/0x1A3, palette 0 slot 1.
rows.why: the flagpole beside the staircase with the flag at its top in this screenshot; CHR $1A2/$1A3 render as the one-pixel shaft halves, $12F/$13D as the ball halves, sprite $7E/$7F as the pennant

rows.name: flagpole ball
rows.notes: World 1-1 end-of-level flagpole, ball on top of the pole - LEFT half (the half to the left of the pole line). CHR $12F is a quarter-round: index-3 black outline with index-1 lime fill and index-2 green shading occupying the right side of the tile, i.e. the left half of a ball whose centre is on the pole line. Nametable tile id $2F at the flagpole's tile column 12 in the single row above the shaft (nametable row 5); palette 0 (slot1 $29 lime, slot2 $1A green, slot3 $0F outline). PROOF: read_nametable 0 (12,3) 3x18 row 5 = 2F 3D 24; get_region object mode at (228,44) selected background palette 0 slots 1,2,3 across CHR 0x12F,0x13D,0x1A2,0x1A3 with box (228,40)-(235,75) (the ball merges into the shaft below it); read_tile 303 = $12F shows the ball's left half.
rows.why: the flagpole beside the staircase with the flag at its top in this screenshot; CHR $1A2/$1A3 render as the one-pixel shaft halves, $12F/$13D as the ball halves, sprite $7E/$7F as the pennant

rows.name: flagpole ball
rows.notes: World 1-1 end-of-level flagpole, ball on top of the pole - RIGHT half. CHR $13D is the mirror of $12F: index-3 black outline with index-2 green and index-1 lime fill on the left side of the tile (the right half of the ball). Nametable tile id $3D at the flagpole's tile column 13 in nametable row 5, palette 0. PROOF: read_nametable 0 (12,3) 3x18 row 5 = 2F 3D 24; get_region object mode at (228,44) listed CHR 0x12F and 0x13D (background palette 0, slots 1,2,3, box (228,40)-(235,75)); read_tile 317 = $13D shows the ball's right half. The pole itself is the pair $1A2/$1A3 read as 'flagpole shaft'.
rows.why: the flagpole beside the staircase with the flag at its top in this screenshot; CHR $1A2/$1A3 render as the one-pixel shaft halves, $12F/$13D as the ball halves, sprite $7E/$7F as the pennant

rows.name: flagpole flag (the pennant on the pole, resting at the top)
rows.notes:
World 1-1 end-of-level flag: the pennant attached to the top of the flagpole is a SPRITE, drawn from SPRITE pattern table $0000, not a background tile. It is a 16x16 metasprite occupying box (216,49)-(231,64) in the frame where it was captured (pole line at x 231-232), i.e. it hangs to the LEFT of the pole. All OAM entries use SPRITE PALETTE 5 (attr low bits = 1). OAM entries (tile id, x/y offset from the box origin, flips):
- #28 $7E (126), (+0,+0), no flips - upper-left
- #29 $7F (127), (+8,+0), no flips - upper-right
- #30 $7E (126), (+8,+8), no flips - lower-right
read_tile $7E = a solid index-2 triangle (full top edge, narrowing to the bottom-right); read_tile $7F = an index-2 field with an index-1 pattern (a small emblem). Sprite palette 5 live = [$0F,$1A,$30,$27] (slot1 $1A green, slot2 $30 white, slot3 $27 orange), so the pennant renders white ($30, index 2) with green ($1A, index 1) detail - sampled get_pixel_color(228,52) = rgb(255,254,255) = $20 white? no: rendered white. PROOF: get_region object mode at (228,52) returned layer 'sprite', palette 5, slots 1+2, 136 connected pixels, bbox (216,49)-(231,64), tiles [126,127], oam [28,29,30]; list_sprites confirms the three entries (215/216,49) tile $7E, (224,49) tile $7F, (224,57) tile $7E, all palette 5; the pole and its ball next to it are BACKGROUND (CHR $1A2/$1A3 and $12F/$13D). The flagpole object itself is the enemy-slot 5 object with Enemy_ID $30 ($001B = 48).
rows.why: the flagpole beside the staircase with the flag at its top in this screenshot; CHR $1A2/$1A3 render as the one-pixel shaft halves, $12F/$13D as the ball halves, sprite $7E/$7F as the pennant
